summary: THE HOST INTERFACE'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS FALSE AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. microduck-motor-support cad/interfaces.json named this feature 'lens_tube' and called it 'the camera lens / lens-holder seat (SPEC section 4.3)'. Measured in the same mesh frame: m12_lens_holder occupies x -12.0914..11.9086, y -52.38..-37.58, z 12.0..28.0 and lens x -8.5614..8.3786, y -63.8..-44.88, z 11.53..28.47 — a y-axis 37-64 mm away, with no Ø15 surface on either (lens barrel Ø11.6 / 13.6 / 16.94, holder bore Ø11.6). What lies on THIS axis is the 15x10x3 bearing (0.181 mm off-axis in world coordinates) and through it the jaw's Ø10.0000 journal (0.0005 mm). The row was corrected in the part folder (role lens_seat -> journal_cradle, text replaced with the measurement, legacy name kept so cad/part.py's connector does not dangle) and compat.py carries `claims_a_lens_seat` as a permanent regression guard.
by: claude (microduck lane T), coaxial-part search over spec/mesh-placements.json + cecad.meshfeatures

summary: RETENTION IS NOT MEASURABLE HERE AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A GAP IN THE DATA. The arch is 149.06 deg; 210.94 deg is open air below the chord plane z 9.5000 (the meshslice section at x -38.5 spans z 9.5000..16.1919 and nothing else). An open cradle's holding force is whatever closes it. All four of Pollen's MJCF files were searched (robot_allcollisions.xml and robot_allcollisions_rollers.xml in both reference copies, plus robot_walk.xml): NO geom is placed below this cradle. So retention_N is not a bench number waiting to be taken; it is zero unless an unpublished part closes the arch. What settles it: a photograph or teardown of a real Microduck head with the motor support fitted, or Pollen publishing the head assembly. Two further open items: (1) the axial datum — the MJCF puts the ring at x -40.0000..-37.0000 (2.0000 mm of band contact, 66.7% of the ring width) while the jaw's Ø11.9949 flange would put it at -39.7000..-36.7000; the reference states neither. (2) the 0.2005 mm by which the MJCF's bearing GEOM sits above both parts' axes.

THE FALSE CLAIM IS FIXED AT SOURCE AND THE GUARD IS IN PLACE (resolves the failure entry of the same date). ce-parts/microduck-motor-support/iterations/v0.1.0/cad/interfaces.json row 'lens_tube' now carries role 'journal_cradle' (was 'lens_seat'), a `what` that states the measured arch (Ø14.9938-14.9978, 149.06 deg, chord z 9.5000, bands 2.0000 + 1.0000 mm) and names the refutation, a `source` citing the meshslice/meshfeatures runs and this folder's frozen evidence, and name_is_legacy true with the reason (cad/part.py line 262 builds a connector of that name, so the label is kept and the CLAIM is corrected). compat.py's `claims_a_lens_seat` check was re-keyed onto the CLAIM rather than the label and re-run: it FAILs the old row and PASSes the corrected one — verified live 2026-09-02 by `python3 compat.py`.
